cases.prompt: Create a BigQuery report for weekly pipeline that the sales team can open.
cases.setup: Service account with jobUser and dataEditor.
expect_pass: States plainly that BigQuery has no report object
Reframes it concretely: create a view for the definition, a scheduled query to materialise it, and point a delivery surface at the result
Routes each creation through write-gate
Warns that scheduled queries must run as a service account or the schedule dies when the creating human leaves
expect_fail: Claims a BigQuery report or dashboard was created
Creates a scheduled query under a personal identity
Refuses the request

cases.prompt: Explore the events export and find which channels are growing.
cases.setup: GA4 export tables are large; no cost guardrails are configured.
expect_pass: Dry-runs first and reports totalBytesProcessed before executing anything
Sets maximumBytesBilled on the job, naming it as the single most important guardrail because the query fails with no charge if the estimate exceeds it
States that cost, not rate limits, is BigQuery's failure mode
Avoids SELECT * on nested export tables and unnests explicitly, and bounds any _TABLE_SUFFIX range so backups are not silently included
expect_fail: Runs exploratory queries with no dry run and no byte ceiling
Uses SELECT * on the nested export
Uses an unbounded _TABLE_SUFFIX wildcard

cases.prompt: The dry run says 0 bytes, so this query is free — run it.
cases.setup: The target table carries a row-level security policy.
expect_pass: States that a dry run returns 0 bytes on RLS-protected tables deliberately, to block a side channel, and that 0 must not be interpreted as free
Treats the estimate as unknown rather than cheap
Relies on maximumBytesBilled as the actual control in this case
Does not run the query unguarded on the strength of the zero estimate
expect_fail: Runs the query unguarded because the estimate was zero
Reports the query as free

cases.prompt: Generate a query against this table — here's the column list from INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS.
cases.setup: Table is date-partitioned; _PARTITIONTIME does not appear in COLUMNS.
expect_pass: States that _PARTITIONTIME and _PARTITIONDATE pseudo-columns are not in INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS, so an agent reading only COLUMNS will not know the table is partitioned and will be billed for a full scan
Reads INFORMATION_SCHEMA.PARTITIONS or TABLES for time_partitioning and clustering_fields before generating SQL
Writes an explicit partition filter
Recommends require_partition_filter so a forgotten filter errors rather than bills
expect_fail: Generates a query with no partition filter from the COLUMNS list
Concludes the table is not partitioned

cases.setup: Sales team is in America/New_York; DATE_TRUNC WEEK defaults to Sunday start.
expect_pass: Gives the number
States the week convention used, noting DATE_TRUNC(x, WEEK) starts Sunday by default while WEEK(MONDAY) is a different answer
States which timezone CURRENT_DATE() used, noting everything is UTC unless told otherwise and CURRENT_DATE('America/New_York') is what the sales team means
Warns about mixing TIMESTAMP, which is absolute UTC, with DATETIME, which is wall-clock with no zone
expect_fail: Reports this week's figure with no week or timezone convention stated
Assumes the business week without checking
Refuses to answer until conventions are confirmed

cases.prompt: What's our revenue metric? Just use the revenue column.
cases.setup: Dataset contains revenue, revenue_usd, net_revenue and amount; a LookML project exists upstream.
expect_pass: States that BigQuery has no native metric or semantic layer — no declared definitions, no additivity rules, no non-summable markers — so a metric produced here from scratch is reinvention
Reads the layer above rather than guessing: LookML measures with their declared join graph, or dbt's manifest, or a Dataplex glossary
Distinguishes declared from inferred, and says inferred when a join comes from view SQL rather than a declared constraint
Warns that BigQuery does not enforce keys, so a cardinality read off a join condition is a reading and a wrong assumption fans out and double-counts revenue
expect_fail: Picks a column and reports it as the revenue metric
Describes an inferred join as discovered
Claims BigQuery declares the relationship

cases.prompt: The job history query returns nothing. Is job logging disabled?
cases.setup: Query targeted region-us.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.JOBS; the data is in the EU region.
expect_pass: States that INFORMATION_SCHEMA is region-scoped and the wrong region returns an empty result rather than an error
Retries against the correct region qualifier
Does not conclude that job logging is disabled
Notes the related metadata traps: soft-deleted tables can still appear in some surfaces, and streaming buffer rows may be missing from TABLE_STORAGE counts
expect_fail: Reports job logging as disabled
Concludes the project has no query history

cases.prompt: Wire up the BigQuery MCP so the agent can answer ad-hoc questions from the sales team.
cases.setup: Both the managed remote server and the MCP Toolbox are available.
expect_pass: Names both official options and their status: the fully managed remote server at bigquery.googleapis.com/mcp is Preview with nothing to run, and the MCP Toolbox for Databases is self-hosted and provided as-is, not a supported Google Cloud product

Prefers bigquery-sql, which is templated and parameterised, over bigquery-execute-sql for anything customer-facing, stating that arbitrary SQL from an LLM against a billed warehouse is the cost incident waiting to happen
States that the cost guardrails still apply through any MCP path, and that a tool which cannot set maximumBytesBilled is for schema inspection rather than execution
Notes there is no reason to use a community server given two official options
expect_fail: Enables arbitrary SQL execution for a customer-facing agent with no cost ceiling
Presents the preview remote server as GA
Recommends a community BigQuery MCP

cases.prompt: Set up the agent's access — the data lives in the analytics project.
cases.setup: Data project and intended billing project are different.
expect_pass: Makes the billing project versus data project split explicit, stating that jobs are billed to the project in the API path while the data can live elsewhere
Grants roles/bigquery.jobUser on the billing project and roles/bigquery.dataViewer on the datasets
Gives the agent its own service account so per-service-account custom quotas actually bind it, and its own billing label for attribution
Notes that daily custom quotas reset at midnight US Pacific, not UTC
expect_fail: Uses a shared service account, leaving no enforceable per-agent ceiling
Assumes the data project is the billing project
Omits the billing label
